effect_estimate.comment: Exact 95% confidence intervals and p-values for regression IRRs are displayed graphically in Fig. 8 (PDF p. 7) and placed in Supplementary Tables 5 and 6 rather than printed numerically in the main text.
effect_estimate.value: Unincorporated communities have higher unserved land area than incorporated communities: on average, nearly 30% of unincorporated community land area is unsewered vs. 11% in incorporated communities (median unsewered area: 15% in Islands, 3.7% in Fringes, 3.1% in Outlying, ~0% in Incorporated; in the highest poverty tercile >=20.5% below poverty, median unsewered area is 19.0% for Islands and 11.8% for Outlying vs. 4.5% for Fringe and 0% for Incorporated). In multilevel negative binomial regressions (N = 31,383 block groups), among high-poverty block groups (>=20% below Federal poverty line), unincorporated status is associated with IRR = 3.54 times greater unsewered land area and IRR = 17.8 times more land area unserved by centralized water relative to incorporated block groups (vs. IRR = 1.48 for unsewered area among block groups without high poverty). Without poverty interactions, Island communities have the largest IRR for unsewered area (IRR = 2.47) and Outlying communities have the largest IRR for area unserved by centralized water (IRR = 5.53); with poverty interactions, high-poverty Outlying and Island block groups both exceed IRR = 4.0 for unsewered area (whereas non-high-poverty Outlying block groups have IRR = 0.91).
effect_estimate.where_found: PDF p. 5-8, Results (Summary statistics, Regression results, Fig. 6-8) & Discussion

mechanism_certainty.comment: Cross-sectional spatial regression design (appraised with JBI Analytical Cross Sectional Checklist, ceiling = 2) quantifying the statistical and spatial association between municipal incorporation status (including 1.6 km municipal extraterritorial jurisdiction buffers) and water/sewer service coverage across block groups; specific administrative processes (e.g., selective annexation/underbounding decisions, extraterritorial planning actions, funding denials) are discussed from statutory/secondary context rather than directly observed in primary administrative records, meriting 1 (documented association).

sample_size.comment: Primary analytic sample is 31,383 Census block groups in 9 states (83% incorporated; ~6% Island, ~8% Fringe, and n = 845 [2.7%] Outlying unincorporated block groups), constructed from 10,948 CWS, 5,220 POTWs (8 states), and 9,087,949 Florida residential parcels; auxiliary radius-prediction models used 1,712 Tier 1 sewer service areas (8 states) and 18,271 Tier 1 water service areas (21 states).
sample_size.value: 31,383 Census block groups across 9 U.S. states (incorporating service areas of 10,948 community water systems in 9 states, 5,220 publicly-owned treatment works in 8 states, and 9,087,949 residential parcels in Florida)

study_design.comment: Combines spatial building footprints (Microsoft/Bing), 2010 Census TIGER/Line municipal boundaries, digitized and approximated utility service area boundaries, 2010 Decennial Census data, and 2008-2012 ACS 5-year poverty estimates in cross-sectional multilevel negative binomial GLMs.
study_design.value: Observational cross-sectional spatial/ecological study at the Census block group level using multilevel Negative Binomial Generalized Linear Models (GLM) with county and state random effects
